user.title: Connect BLUETTI on your local network
user.description: Read-only local monitoring. Automatic: Home Assistant on the Linux router. Direct DNS: LAN connection through local DNS, including a separate Home Assistant host; requires router DNS/DHCP setup. Manual: keep the existing router path. No cloud account or Bluetooth.

network.title: Configure this UPS’s network
network.description: Home Assistant must run on the UPS’s Linux router. Three redirects are scoped to {device_ip} and {receiver_ip}. Two fresh reports are required within three minutes. Stop, reload, disable or removal deletes its rules. No permanent Internet block or AC/DC commands.

data.confirm: I confirm the topology and UPS-only rules

direct_dns.title: Direct DNS and LAN connection
direct_dns.description: UPS {device_ip} must resolve the four BLUETTI names to {receiver_ip} and connect on port 18760. Choose an existing local resolver or built-in DNS on port 53. The built-in listener serves only this UPS: assign it only to that device via DHCP, without a router DNS proxy. With an external resolver, rewrite iot.bluettipower.com, gw.bluettipower.com, gwpry.bluettipower.com and iotde.bluettipower.com. The MQTT receiver is inside the integration. No permanent Internet block is created.

data.confirm_dns: I configured DNS/DHCP so this UPS connects to the local receiver
